method: Each entry below was retrieved directly from the publisher's own domain on 2026-11-10 during this session. The 'verifies' field lists only what the retrieved text actually supports. Nothing is inferred.

irs_estate.title: Estate tax (filing threshold table, portability)
verifies: Federal estate-tax filing threshold for 2026 is $15,000,000 (table lists 2011-2026)
Filing is required when gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts plus specific gift exemption exceeds the year-of-death threshold
A surviving spouse may receive unused exclusion only through a timely estate-tax return election
irs_estate.quote: 2026 | $15,000,000 ... A filing is required if the gross estate of the decedent, increased by the decedent's adjusted taxable gifts and specific gift tax exemption, is valued at more than the filing threshold for the year of the decedent's death

irs_estate_faq.title: Frequently asked questions on estate taxes
verifies: Public Law 119-21 amended IRC 2010(c)(3) to increase the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026
Form 706 is due nine months after death; an automatic six-month extension is available by filing Form 4768
Portability requires a timely filed Form 706
irs_estate_faq.quote: The Working Families Tax Cuts Bill was signed into law on July 4, 2025 as Public Law 119-21 and amends 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for gifts for calendar year 2026.

irs_basis.title: Gifts & inheritances (basis of inherited property)
verifies: Basis of inherited property is generally fair market value on the date of death, whether or not Form 706 is filed
Alternate valuation is available only if the executor files Form 706 and elects it
Gain above basis on a later sale is taxable
The annual gift exclusion is $19,000 for 2025 and 2026
irs_basis.quote: The basis of property inherited from a decedent is generally ... The fair market value (FMV) of the property on the date of the decedent's death

irs_tc409.title: Topic no. 409, Capital gains and losses
verifies: Long-term capital gain is taxed at 0%, 15%, or 20% depending on taxable income (2025 thresholds shown)
A 20% rate applies to the extent taxable income exceeds the 15% thresholds
A net investment income tax may additionally apply (see Topic 559)
irs_tc409.quote: However, a capital gains rate of 20% applies to the extent that your taxable income exceeds the thresholds set for the 15% capital gain rate.

irs_tc701.title: Topic no. 701, Sale of your home
verifies: Up to $250,000 of gain ($500,000 on a joint return) may be excluded on the sale of a main home
Ownership and use tests are generally 24 months out of the last 5 years
irs_tc701.quote: you may qualify to exclude up to $250,000 of that gain from your income, or up to $500,000 of that gain if you file a joint return with your spouse

boe_prop19.title: Proposition 19 (RTC 63.2) comparison tables and filing deadlines
verifies: The family-home exclusion applies only where the property is the principal residence of both transferor and transferee
Effective February 16, 2021; implemented by Revenue & Taxation Code 63.2
Transferee must file for the homeowners' exemption within 1 year of transfer and claim the exclusion within 3 years or before transfer to a third party
boe_prop19.quote: File for homeowners' exemption within 1 year of transfer - File claim for exclusion within 3 years or before transfer to third party

boe_cap.title: BOE adjusts the Proposition 19 $1 million intergenerational transfer exclusion amount (NR 25-02)
verifies: The exclusion adjustment is $1,044,590 for transfers February 16, 2025 through February 15, 2027
The excludable amount is the property's factored base year value at transfer plus $1,044,590
The amount is recalculated every other year using the Federal Housing Finance Agency House Price Index for California
boe_cap.quote: The excludable amount is capped at an amount equal to the principal residence or family farm's factored base year value (taxable value) at the time of the transfer plus $1,044,586.

rtc13301.title: Revenue & Taxation Code 13301 - Prohibition of gift and death taxes
verifies: Neither the state nor any political subdivision may impose any gift, inheritance, succession, legacy, income, or estate tax on a transfer occurring by reason of death
Enacted by initiative Proposition 6, June 8, 1982
rtc13301.quote: Neither the state nor any political subdivision of the state shall impose any gift, inheritance, succession, legacy, income, or estate tax, or any other tax, on gifts or on the estate or inheritance of any person or on or by reason of any transfer occurring by reason of a death.

rtc51.title: Revenue & Taxation Code 51 - inflation factor for base year values
verifies: Taxable value is the lesser of the inflation-adjusted base year value or full cash value
The annual inflation increase may not exceed 2 percent of the prior year's value
The inflation factor uses the October-to-October California CPI change
rtc51.quote: In no event shall the percentage increase for any assessment year determined pursuant to subparagraph (A), (B), or (C) exceed 2 percent of the prior year's value.

rtc480.title: Revenue & Taxation Code 480 - change in ownership statement
verifies: Where an interest in real property transfers by reason of death including through a trust, the trustee or transferee files a change in ownership statement within 150 days after the date of death
Failure to file after a written request can trigger a penalty of $100 or 10 percent of the taxes on the new base year value, whichever is greater
rtc480.quote: in all other cases in which an interest in real property is transferred by reason of death, including a transfer through the medium of a trust, the change in ownership statement or statements shall be filed by the trustee (if the property was held in trust) or the transferee with the county recorder or assessor ... within 150 days after the date of death

prob16061.title: Probate Code 16061.7 - notification by trustee
verifies: The trustee must serve a notification when a revocable trust becomes irrevocable because of a settlor's death
The notification must be served not later than 60 days after the event requiring service
Service is on each beneficiary and each heir of the deceased settlor
prob16061.quote: The notification by trustee shall be served not later than 60 days following the occurrence of the event requiring service of the notification by trustee

ftb_rates.title: 2025 California Tax Rate Schedules (Form 540)
verifies: California brackets run from 1.00% to 12.30%
The 12.30% bracket begins at $742,950 of taxable income for single filers and $1,485,900 for joint filers (2025, rounded to $10)

ftb_cg.title: Capital gains and losses
verifies: California has no lower rate for capital gains; capital gains are taxed as ordinary income
ftb_cg.quote: California does not have a lower rate for capital gains. All capital gains are taxed as ordinary income.

sf_rate.title: Resolution 447-25 (File 250876) - FY2025-26 combined property tax rate for jurisdiction B
sf_rate.publisher: Board of Supervisors (jurisdiction B rate-setting authority)
verifies: Combined FY2025-26 property tax rate is $1.18268325 per $100 of taxable property value
The resolution sets only the ad valorem rate; it does not include non-ad-valorem parcel charges
Passed September 30, 2025
sf_rate.quote: the combined property tax rate ... shall therefore be $1.18268325 on each $100 valuation of said taxable property

cpuc_nem.title: Net Energy Metering and Net Billing
verifies: Customers applying for interconnection since April 15, 2023 take service on the net billing tariff under D.22-12-056
Export compensation is usually lower than the retail rate
Legacy NEM tariffs are closed to new enrollments; the NBT legacy period is nine years
End-of-year surplus under NEM is compensated at roughly $0.02-$0.03 per kWh
cpuc_nem.quote: The value of the export compensation (which the IOUs term "Energy Export Credits") is usually lower than the retail rate

cdi_tool.title: Online homeowner insurance pricing tool helps residents find coverage (release 138-18)
verifies: The CDI comparison tool shows each company's average premium, not an actual quote
Consumers enter county and nearest city, coverage type and amount, and home age
The FAIR Plan is available where standard coverage cannot be obtained
cdi_tool.quote: While this tool does not provide actual premium quotes, it does provide each company's average premium

lao_250017.title: LAO analysis of proposed initiative A.G. File No. 25-0017 (property tax rules for inherited property)
verifies: The measure would restore pre-Proposition 19 exclusion rules beginning January 1, 2027
The expanded rules would apply to all inherited primary homes regardless of value
The rules would also apply to properties transferred since February 16, 2021
LAO estimates local revenue losses of about one billion dollars per year initially, growing to about two billion dollars per year
lao_250017.quote: Beginning January 1, 2027, the measure reverses most of the major changes made by Proposition 19.

sos_measures.title: Qualified Statewide Ballot Measures
verifies: The November 3, 2026 statewide ballot contains Propositions 1-5 and 37-45
No inherited-property measure appears among the qualified November 3, 2026 measures listed
sos_measures.quote: ## November 3, 2026, Statewide Ballot Measures ... Proposition 45 ... Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects.

irs_2027.title: IR-2026-133 (Nov 5, 2026): IRS releases tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2027 (Revenue Procedure 2026-35)
verifies: Basic exclusion amount for estates of decedents dying in 2027 is $15,480,000, up from $15,000,000 for 2026
Annual gift-tax exclusion rises to $20,000 per recipient for 2027, up from $19,000 for 2026
Annual exclusion for gifts to a non-citizen spouse rises to $201,000 for 2027, up from $194,000 for 2026
irs_2027.quote: Estates of decedents who die during 2027 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,480,000, up from a total of $15,000,000 for estates of decedents who died in 2026.

sf_treasurer.title: Secured Property Taxes - current secured rate for jurisdiction B (treasurer-tax collector)
verifies: The secured property tax rate for Fiscal Year 2026-27 is 1.18162182%
Secured bills are mailed in October; first installment delinquent after December 10, second after April 10
A change in ownership or new construction triggers a supplemental assessment on the value difference
sf_treasurer.quote: The secured property tax rate for Fiscal Year 2026-27 is 1.18162182%.

sf_rentboard.title: Current rates, including rent increase, relocation, security deposit (jurisdiction B rent board)
verifies: Allowable annual rent increase is 1.6% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027
Prior allowable increases: 1.4% (Mar 2025-Feb 2026) and 1.7% (Mar 2024-Feb 2025)

Notice posted November 9, 2026: the Board of Supervisors is considering File No. 261020, which would temporarily limit combined banked and capital-improvement rent increases to 10% per year for rent-controlled units; not enacted and subject to change
sf_rentboard.quote: Allowable Rent Increase: 1.6% for March 1, 2026 - February 28, 2027

sos_memo.title: CC/ROV Memorandum #26138 (May 18, 2026): Initiative - Failure of 1994, Related to Property Taxes on Transfers Between Family Members
verifies: Initiative 1994 (A.G. File 25-0017), the constitutional amendment repealing Proposition 19's transfer rules, failed: signatures filed were less than 100 percent of the required number (Elections Code section 9030(b))
Title of measure: REPEALS VOTER-ENACTED CHANGES TO PROPERTY TAX RULES FOR TRANSFERS BETWEEN FAMILY MEMBERS. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT. Summary date November 6, 2025
The measure therefore was not on the November 3, 2026 statewide ballot; Proposition 19 rules remain in effect
sos_memo.quote: ...the total number of signatures for the hereinafter named initiative filed with all county elections officials is less than 100 percent of the number of qualified voters required to find the petition sufficient; therefore, the petition has failed.

sb974.title: SB 974, Stats. 2026 ch. 665 - Property taxation: change in ownership: generational transfers: special needs trusts
verifies: Amends Revenue and Taxation Code section 63.2 so a court-established special needs trust must be considered an eligible medium of transfer for the family-home / family-farm exclusion
Approved by the Governor and filed with the Secretary of State on September 27, 2026 (Chapter 665)
No urgency clause, so the general January 1, 2027 effective-date rule applies; all other section 63.2 requirements are unchanged
sb974.quote: This bill would revise the definition of 'transfer' for purposes of the above-described property tax law provisions to require that a special needs trust, established as described above, be considered an eligible medium of transfer.
